subject: Numeracy
title: Days and time
objectives: Children will name parts of the day and days of the week.
Children will use yesterday, today and tomorrow.
content: Morning, afternoon and night, days of the week, and yesterday, today and tomorrow.
teachingActivities: Link time words to the school day and family routines; use a daily timetable with pictures; sing the days of the week song; use a calendar and turn a page each day; keep each idea concrete (what we did yesterday).
learnerActivities: Name parts of the day and days of the week and say yesterday, today and tomorrow.
resources: Pictures of morning, afternoon and night routines
assessment: Observe whether each child names parts of the day and says today and tomorrow correctly with support.
expectedOutcomes: Says today and tomorrow correctly with support.

lessons.title: Morning, afternoon and night
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will name morning, afternoon and night and say what we do in each.
successCriteria: Matches activities to the time of day
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weight and capacity.
resources: Pictures: waking up, school, lunch, sleeping
lessons.starter: Show a sun picture and say "In the morning we wake up. In the afternoon we play. At night we sleep."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say the time of day.
Ask "What do we do in the morning?"
Put activity pictures under the right time.
Sing a song about the day.
learnerActivities: Children repeat morning, afternoon or night.
Child says wake up or go to school.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say the time of day. Children: Children repeat morning, afternoon or night.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What do we do in the morning?" Children: Child says wake up or go to school.
Step 3. Teacher: Put activity pictures under the right time. Children: Child places a picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Sing a song about the day. Children: Children sing with actions.

practical.title: Day pictures
steps: Put it in the right place.
practical.safety: Use gentle pictures and keep the floor clear. Accept different home routines.

differentiation.support: Sort two times of day only.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what they do in each part of the day.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at night?
When do we go to school?

expectedOutcomes: Matches activities to the time of day
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say good morning.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about your family routine through the day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name morning, afternoon and night and say what we do in each" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Days of the week
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say the days of the week in order.
successCriteria: Says the days of the week with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weight and capacity.
lessons.starter: Sing the days of the week song with a clap for each day.
teacherActivities: Teach the song and show each day card.
Put the day cards in order.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Teach the song and show each day card. Children: Children sing and point.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Seven days make a week." Children: Children count seven days.
Step 3. Teacher: Put the day cards in order. Children: Child places a card.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What day is it today?" Children: Child says the day.

practical.title: Days in order
practical.safety: Keep cards on a mat and supervise sharing. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Use three days and say them together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say the days of a whole week without cards.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many days in a week?

expectedOutcomes: Says the days of the week with support
lessons.conclusion: Sing the song once more and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Say the days of the week at the start of each day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say the days of the week in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Seven days in a week, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.

lessons.title: Yesterday, today and tomorrow
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say what happened yesterday, what happens today and what will happen tomorrow.
successCriteria: Matches an activity to the right word
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weight and capacity.
lessons.starter: Say "Yesterday we sang. Today we count. Tomorrow we play."
teacherActivities: Show the calendar and point to yesterday, today and tomorrow.
Talk about what we did yesterday.
Talk about what we will do tomorrow.
Sort pictures into the three baskets.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the words.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the calendar and point to yesterday, today and tomorrow. Children: Children look and say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Talk about what we did yesterday. Children: Child says something from yesterday.
Step 3. Teacher: Talk about what we will do tomorrow. Children: Child says something for tomorrow.
Step 4. Teacher: Sort pictures into the three baskets. Children: Child sorts a picture.

practical.title: Three days
steps: Say what we will do tomorrow.
practical.safety: Keep the sorting seated and gentle. Accept every child’s idea.

differentiation.support: Talk about today and tomorrow only.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what day it was yesterday.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Matches activities to the right word
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about yesterday, today and tomorrow at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say what happened yesterday, what happens today and what will happen tomorrow" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A calendar with three days marked

lessons.title: Our week
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make a picture week showing what happens on each day.
successCriteria: Says what happens on a day
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weight and capacity.
resources: A large week chart with seven boxes
lessons.starter: Show a blank week chart and say "Let us fill in what we do each day."
teacherActivities: Name each day and talk about what we do.
Place picture cards in the day boxes.
Ask "What do we do on Friday?"
learnerActivities: Children say the days and activities.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Name each day and talk about what we do. Children: Children say an activity.
Step 2. Teacher: Place picture cards in the day boxes. Children: Child places a picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Read the chart together. Children: Children say the days and activities.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What do we do on Friday?" Children: Child says the activity.

practical.title: Week chart
practical.safety: Use sticky tack that is safe and keep it away from mouths. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Fill in three days with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what comes after Wednesday.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do on Friday?

expectedOutcomes: Says what happens on a day
lessons.conclusion: Hang the chart and say the days.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a picture week at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a picture week showing what happens on each day" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 time check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses time words.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weight and capacity.
lessons.starter: Sing the days song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: parts of the day, days and yesterday today tomorrow.
At each station ask a time question and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: parts of the day, days and yesterday today tomorrow. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask a time question and watch. Children: Child answers with a word.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Time stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Accept different home routines.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use morning and night.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to say the days in order.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names parts of the day; says days of the week; says yesterday, today and tomorrow; matches activities to times.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep using time words at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses time words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
